free_tier.stated: Free plan at USD 0 with '10k credits per month'. One shared monthly pool across every product, with the vendor's own per-product rates: 'Text to Speech 1 credit per character; Speech to Text 330 credits per minute; Eleven Music 900 credits per minute; Sound Effects 200 credits per generation; Voice Changer and Voice Isolator 1,000 credits per minute'. 10,000 credits therefore buys either 10,000 characters of TTS (about 10 minutes of audio at the common 1,000 characters a minute), or 30 minutes of speech-to-text, or 50 sound effects, or 5 minutes of voice isolation, per month.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: the 10,000 credits compose with a free transcription service by splitting the job: send speech-to-text to a vendor with a larger minute allowance and keep ElevenLabs for the TTS voice, because 330 credits a minute makes this pool the worst value as a transcriber. What breaks: any loop that synthesises more than 10,000 characters a month, which is roughly 10 minutes of speech.

limits.value: the monthly credit pool is small and does not roll over on the Free plan: 'Rollover does not apply to the Free plan', so the 10,000 credits are lost at the end of each billing cycle and a batch job larger than 10 minutes of audio cannot be finished across two months.

notes: These are inference credits, not general compute: no machine, no shell, no GPU is handed over, only metered calls to a hosted voice model. Per-month character cost of the cheapest paid lane for scale: Starter at USD 6 for 30,000 credits is USD 0.20 per 1,000 characters. Open question: whether one email address can hold more than one free workspace; the pricing page does not say and no probe was run against the signup endpoint.
